guide.title: Clinton, Connecticut: Brownstoners, Witch Hazel, and a Harbor
guide.intro: Clinton was established as a separate town in May 1838, broken off from Kenilworth — today's Killingworth — and originally part of the Homonoscitt Plantation, also called Hammonasset. Sitting in Middlesex County at the mouth of the Hammonasset River on Long Island Sound, its early economy was built on maritime trade: local shipyards built schooners called "brownstoners" that carried Portland brownstone down the Connecticut River. In the late nineteenth century, Pond's Extract, distilled from native witch hazel in Clinton, helped give rise to Chesebrough-Pond's, Inc., once the world's largest producer of face creams. Yale University traces its roots here too: the Collegiate School began with one student trained in the Killingworth (now Clinton) home of Rector Abraham Pierson, before moving on to Saybrook and then New Haven. Clinton-born figures include engraver and inventor Abel Buell (1743) and shipping magnate Charles Morgan, one of the era's most esteemed New York millionaires.

sections.heading: Brownstoners and witch hazel
sections.body: Clinton was established as a separate town in May 1838, broken off from Kenilworth — today's Killingworth — and originally part of the Homonoscitt Plantation, also called Hammonasset. Sitting at the mouth of the Hammonasset River on Long Island Sound, its early economy was built on maritime trade: local shipyards built schooners called "brownstoners" that carried Portland brownstone down the Connecticut River. In the late nineteenth century, Pond's Extract, distilled from native witch hazel in Clinton, became a signature product that helped give rise to Chesebrough-Pond's, Inc., described as the world's largest producer of face creams. Yale University traces its origins here too: the Collegiate School began with one student trained in the home of Rector Abraham Pierson of Killingworth (now Clinton), before the school relocated to Saybrook and later New Haven. Engraver and inventor Abel Buell was born in Clinton in 1743, and shipping and railroad magnate Charles Morgan, one of the most esteemed New York millionaires of the nineteenth century, also had roots in the town.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Most visitors drive Interstate 95 along the shoreline — Clinton Premium Outlets sits directly off it, near the CT-81/Killingworth Turnpike interchange — with US Route 1 running through the town center as East/West Main Street. Car-free travelers can take CTrail Shore Line East commuter rail to Clinton station at 10 John Street Extension, which has free daily parking, accessible level-boarding platforms, and River Valley Transit bus connections; the station is on the same New Haven-New London line that also serves Old Saybrook.

sections.heading: Outlets, a harbor, and a stone house
sections.body: The Adam Stanton House and General Store, built in 1791 and left in trust as a public museum in 1916, preserves original Stanton family furnishings, clothing, documents, and general-store inventory. Clinton Town Beach, on Clinton Harbor, has walkable sandbars at low tide, a car-top kayak launch, and a fishing walkway over the Hammock River; beach passes are required from the third weekend of June through Labor Day. Clinton Premium Outlets, more than 70 stores along I-95, is one of the shoreline's best-known shopping stops. For dinner, Chamard Vineyards' farm-to-table bistro, Chips' Pub III (serving Clinton since 1994), and the Clinton location of Westbrook Lobster are all verified options. No hotel, inn, or B&B physically in Clinton could be verified as operating in 2026; the nearest confirmed option is Water's Edge Resort & Spa, one town east in Westbrook.

faq.question: How do I get to Clinton?
faq.answer: Drivers use I-95 or US Route 1 (East/West Main Street). Clinton's own Shore Line East station (10 John Street Extension) has free daily parking, level boarding, and River Valley Transit bus connections.

faq.question: Does the train from Clinton go to New York?
faq.answer: No. Shore Line East runs between New Haven Union Station and New London, so there is no direct New York service from Clinton; the station is for travel along the Connecticut shoreline.

faq.question: What is the Adam Stanton House?
faq.answer: A 1791 merchant's house and general store left in trust by the Stanton family's heirs in 1916 to operate as a public museum, preserving original furnishings and store inventory. Tours by appointment.

faq.question: What are the rules for Clinton Town Beach?
faq.answer: Beach passes are required 9 a.m.-5 p.m. from Memorial Day through Labor Day, with a gatekeeper on duty 9 a.m.-3 p.m.; from the third weekend of June through Labor Day, access is pass-holders only.

faq.question: Where can I stay near Clinton?
faq.answer: No hotel, inn, or B&B in Clinton itself could be verified as operating in 2026. The nearest confirmed option is Water's Edge Resort & Spa in Westbrook, one town east on US-1.

faq.question: What is Clinton Premium Outlets?
faq.answer: An outdoor village-style outlet center off I-95 with more than 70 designer and name-brand stores, including Coach, Polo Ralph Lauren, and Michael Kors, advertising everyday savings of 25%-65%.

places.name: Adam Stanton House and General Store
places.summary: Built in 1791 by a wealthy merchant-businessman; in 1916 Adam Stanton's heirs left the house in trust to operate as a public museum, preserving original Stanton family furnishings, clothing, documents, and general-store inventory depicting 18th- and 19th-century New England life. Tours by appointment.

places.name: Clinton Town Beach
places.summary: A sandy town beach on Clinton Harbor facing Long Island Sound, with walkable sandbars at low tide, car-top launch access for sea kayaks, a fishing walkway along an old stone bridge over the Hammock River, and seasonal concessions and restrooms. Beach passes required 9 a.m.-5 p.m. Memorial Day through Labor Day, with a gatekeeper on duty 9 a.m.-3 p.m.; from the third weekend of June through Labor Day, access is pass-holders only.

places.name: Clinton Premium Outlets (Clinton Crossing)
places.summary: An outdoor village-style outlet center along I-95 with more than 70 designer and name-brand stores (Coach, Polo Ralph Lauren, Nike Factory Store, Saks OFF 5TH, Michael Kors, among others), advertising everyday savings of 25%-65%. Regular hours from April 1; reduced winter (Jan-Mar) schedule.

places.name: Chamard Vineyards Farm Winery Bistro
places.summary: A working farm, winery, and farm-to-table bistro with vineyard views, pairing its cuisine with Chamard's own wines; Wednesday-Thursday 4-6 p.m. happy hour. Hours Wednesday-Saturday 12-9, Sunday 11-5.

places.name: Chips' Pub III
places.summary: A local institution serving the Clinton community since 1994 — an American restaurant and pub with a nautical Irish/English-pub feel, known for burgers, fish tacos, steaks, seafood, and wings. Daily 11:30 a.m.-10 p.m., indoor and outdoor dining.

places.name: Westbrook Lobster Restaurant (Clinton)
places.summary: Despite the name, this longtime shoreline seafood restaurant's flagship location is in Clinton, with a second location in Wallingford; reservations for the Clinton dining room are taken through Resy.
